_comment: Deliberately broken items. Each one exists to prove a specific gate fires;
pipeline/test/validator.test.js asserts on the codes below. Nothing here is
correct Luxembourgish - do not copy anything out of this file.
Every 'bad' string is a one-character-class corruption of a real LOD sentence,
so a gate that passes it is a gate that would pass a real authoring mistake.

items.notes: expects lexicon/unknown - 'Aarbescht' is a deliberate misspelling of 'Aarbecht' (AARBECHT1)
items.transcript: huet däi Brudder endlech eng Aarbescht fonnt?
items.question_en: Control: this sentence is LOD verbatim except for one corrupted noun.

items.notes: expects lexicon/erroneous - LOD itself flags this spelling as wrong
items.question_en: Control: a spelling LOD explicitly marks reason="erroneous-spelling".

items.notes: expects n-rule/keep - LOD writes 'ech maache reegelméisseg Sport'; the n must drop before the s
expects audio/unresolved - the id is not a recording in corpus.json
items.transcript: an zwou Wochen ass endlech Vakanz!
items.question_en: Control: valid Luxembourgish, dangling audio reference.

items.notes: expects schema/unknown-field - an unclassified field would otherwise skip validation entirely
items.subtitle: eng Aarbescht ouni Kontroll
items.question_en: Control: text smuggled into a field the validator does not know about.
